title: Best Microwaves UK
short: Solo, grill and combi microwaves compared by cooking performance, capacity and features, from budget flatbed models to premium air-fry combis.
intro: A microwave's real test is how evenly it heats and defrosts, not just its headline wattage. This guide compares microwaves tested by Trusted Reviews using a thermal camera to check even heating, alongside real tasks like defrosting bread and cooking jacket potatoes.

products.name: Combi Wave 3 in 1
products.best_for: Buyers who want a microwave, air fryer and oven combined
products.key_spec: 32L capacity, air fry, oven and grill modes, six function buttons
products.summary: Trusted Reviews found this performed admirably across nearly every function, cooking a jacket potato in under seven minutes and a 1.6kg roast chicken using combined microwave, oven and grill modes. Air fry mode gave evenly browned, crispy chips with a helpful stir reminder halfway through, though it's large and expensive.

specs.Functions: Fast Combi, Air Fry, Oven, Microwave, Grill

pros: Genuinely versatile (air fryer, oven, grill, microwave)

products.name: MS32DG4504ATE3 Large Capacity Solo Microwave
products.best_for: Larger households who need to heat a lot of food at once
products.key_spec: 32L capacity, claimed enough for 5kg of potatoes, Deodorisation programme
products.summary: Trusted Reviews was seriously impressed by consistent results across both conventional and difficult tasks, defrosting chicken in around 10 minutes and salmon in just 7.5. Bacon reached piping hot in 45 seconds, though the huge dimensions demand serious counter space and it only offers basic functionality for the price.
cons: Large dimensions need generous counter space

products.name: NN-CS89LBBPQ Combination Microwave Oven
products.best_for: Buyers who want an oven-like microwave with self-cleaning
products.key_spec: Flatbed design, 3 tray slots, self-cleaning steam function, humidity auto-sensor
products.summary: The most generous oven space Trusted Reviews has seen in a microwave, with three tray slots for cooking multiple items and auto programmes handling up to 2kg of meat. A humidity-sensing combi programme delivered a jacket potato with crispy skin and fluffy centre, though the touch controls aren't very intuitive and results can be uneven.
pros: Versatile auto programmes for defrosting, steaming, grilling, roasting

products.name: Easy View Convection Oven with HotBlast Technology MC28M6075CS
products.best_for: Buyers who want the microwave to work out settings for them
products.summary: Samsung's Sensor cooking mode measures gasses released from food to stop cooking at the optimal point, giving Trusted Reviews a jacket potato that was fluffy inside and cooked through. Automatic defrost programmes worked well too, though HotBlast convection results don't quite match a dedicated air fryer for crispiness.

specs.Modes: Sensor cooking, HotBlast convection, auto defrost

pros: Can do many jobs a full oven can
cons: Needs space for all the accessories
products.search: Samsung Easy View HotBlast MC28M6075CS microwave

products.name: MCG 25 Ceramic Chef Microwave
products.best_for: Buyers who want to fit larger or odd-shaped dishes without a turntable
products.key_spec: 25L flatbed capacity, grill and convection oven modes, wire shelf and baking tray included
products.summary: A flatbed design that Trusted Reviews found gave even heating with no cold spots on basic tasks, and worked well combining grill and microwave modes together. The convection oven setting performed admirably too, though the interface takes getting used to and the standalone grill wasn't particularly even.

products.name: Design MG 20 Ecostyle Ceramic Microwave & Grill
products.best_for: Buyers who want flatbed practicality on a tight budget
products.key_spec: 20L flatbed capacity, 5 power levels, grill and 3 combi modes
products.summary: A rare flatbed microwave for just over £100, with no turntable meaning more usable internal space for rectangular dishes and easier cleaning. Trusted Reviews found microwave performance convincing, with rice heating evenly and a fluffy baked potato centre, though there are no automated programmes and the grill runs hot enough to catch food at the edges.
pros: Cooks well on standard microwave mode
cons: No automated programmes, manual timing needed

products.name: Cassini 20L Digital Microwave
products.best_for: Small households who want a simple, good-looking microwave
products.key_spec: 20L capacity, digital controls, dimpled fingerprint-resistant finish
products.summary: Trusted Reviews picked this for small households wanting something straightforward and good-looking, available in green, black or blue with a dimpled finish that resists fingerprints. Digital controls and a useful defrost mode cover the essentials well, though you can't add extra cooking time partway through a cycle.

guide.a: A solo microwave just heats and defrosts. A grill microwave adds browning and crisping via a heating element. A combi microwave, like the Sage Combi Wave or Panasonic here, adds a convection oven mode too, letting it roast and bake much like a full oven, at a higher price.

guide.q: Does a flatbed microwave actually cook better than a turntable one?
guide.a: Not necessarily better, but flatbed microwaves like the Caso models here offer more usable internal space since there's no rotating plate to work around, making it easier to fit rectangular or oversized dishes. Even heating still depends on the specific model's design, not just the absence of a turntable.

A 20L microwave suits one or two people and everyday reheating. Larger households, or anyone wanting to cook bigger dishes or use a full dinner plate comfortably, should look at 28-32L models like the Samsung or Sage here, but check they'll actually fit your counter space first.

guide.q: Are automated sensor cooking programmes worth it?
guide.a: Automated programmes, like Samsung's Sensor cooking here, remove the guesswork of choosing power and time for specific foods, which is genuinely useful for jacket potatoes or defrosting. They add cost though, so they're most worth it if you regularly cook a variety of different foods rather than just reheating the same few meals.
